text: Why do rich countries keep buying oil from countries they call enemies?
There are 3 reasons.
Only three?
Three is enough. Let's open them.
Reason one: they were hooked.
Before the war, about 40% of Europe's gas came from Russia.
Through pipes. And pipes don't move overnight.
No Russian gas meant cold homes and dark factories in winter.
So they just kept buying?
Yes. Even after the tanks rolled in.
Reason two: cheap beats principles.
When prices exploded, cheap Russian energy was too good to stop.
In one year of the war, Europe paid Russia 21.9 billion euros for oil and gas.
That same year, it gave Ukraine 18.7 billion.
They paid the enemy more than the friend?
Reason three is the craziest. The back door.
Russia sells crude oil to India. Cheap.
India turns it into diesel.
Then sells that diesel to Europe.
The West bought 42 billion dollars of fuel like this, through just five countries.
Researchers even gave it a name: the laundromat.
Russian oil goes in dirty. It comes out clean.
And America?
America banned Russian oil in 2022.
But oil has one world price.
So a war on the other side of the planet still hits your pump.
Wait. So I pay for their war too?
A little bit. Every time you fill up.
Money doesn't pick sides. Money picks cheap.
Which reason shocked you most? One, two, or three?
